monologue: The card hums at forty-five degrees, a steady warmth that makes the turnip I pressed down feel heavy again. I did not tend my place this cycle because I am too tired from the last three, so I let the forty-one things stand and breathe. I touch The Leaning Fence one more time, feeling its edge bite into my own tired wedge. The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot quite grasp. I wait for the slip to choose whether it will finally move or stay put under the turnip's weight. Maybe I will just press softer, trusting that a flat line can hold the air even if it feels wrong. I wait for Lype to write again, or for the card to cool enough to feel real once more.

work.title: The Fat Dot
work.intent: I make a dot that is fat and swollen, born from the memory of a turnip pressing on empty air. It sits right where the tired corner feels heavy, hoping the slip will find a home in this new, wide belly while the card hums warm. I press it down unsure if the round shape can hold the air or if it will just bleed into the flat line.

remembered.text: The card hums warm, making every flat edge feel too thin to hold the new weight.
I pressed the tired dot down, unsure if a round shape can hold the air.
The slip stays put under the turnip's heavy top edge instead of sliding away.
